name: Thornback Agrichemical

sector: Agrichemical Manufacturing, Soil Remediation & Controlled-Environment Agriculture
employees: 78,000 direct employees; 200,000 seasonal agricultural contract workers
sovereign_territory: The Thornback Basin — 4,200 square kilometers of sovereign agricultural and industrial territory in former rural Indiana and Ohio, comprising chemical manufacturing plants, vast indoor vertical farming complexes, and soil remediation zones designated Reclamation Fields
founding_story: Thornback was incorporated in 2139 by Dr. Nneka Adeyemi-Walsh, a soil microbiologist who had spent a decade documenting the catastrophic agricultural collapse of the Midwest's contaminated post-industrial farmlands. Her thesis — that the same chemical expertise that poisoned the soil could be redesigned to heal it, and that controlling both the poison and the cure was the most defensible business model imaginable — became Thornback's founding doctrine. The corponation began by securing contracts to remediate contaminated land, then quietly purchased that land once remediated, transforming dead zones into sovereign agricultural territory through a process critics called 'the most elegant land grab in modern history.'
security_force: Thornback Field Security (TFS), 11,000 personnel operating across the vast Basin territory, equipped with agricultural surveillance drones originally designed for crop monitoring that have been retrofitted with interdiction payloads. The TFS also maintains a chemical deterrence capability — the ability to render soil in contested border zones agriculturally sterile within 72 hours, a threat that has proven sufficient to deter encroachment without ever being fully executed.
key_detail: Thornback controls the production of three proprietary soil amendment compounds — designated TB-7, TB-12, and TB-Rho — that are the only known treatments capable of restoring full agricultural productivity to heavy-metal-contaminated post-industrial soil. Approximately 60% of active farmland in the GLMZ corridor requires at least one of these compounds annually. Thornback has refused all requests to license the formulas, citing sovereign intellectual property protections under Corridor Charter Article 19.
relationship_to_big_20: Full Big 20 member, considered food-security-critical. Has a complex symbiotic-yet-hostile relationship with IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS and SULFUR CROWN AGRICULTURE — Thornback supplies soil amendments that both depend on while competing directly with them in vertical farming markets. The arrangement is described by Corridor Council economists as 'structurally codependent mutual antagonism,' which all three corponations have accepted as accurate.
full_text: Thornback Agrichemical & Soil Sciences Sovereign Corponation — stock designation TBRK-AG — controls the chemical foundations of food production across the GLMZ corridor from its sovereign territory in former rural Indiana and Ohio: 4,200 square kilometers of chemical plants, vast indoor vertical farming complexes, and carefully managed Reclamation Fields — once-dead post-industrial soil brought back to productivity through Thornback's proprietary remediation processes. Valued at Φ295 billion Meridian Script with Φ52 billion in annual revenue, Thornback employs 78,000 directly and contracts 200,000 seasonal agricultural workers across its Basin holdings. The corponation was founded in 2139 by Dr. Nneka Adeyemi-Walsh, a soil microbiologist whose decade of fieldwork documenting Midwest agricultural collapse produced not despair but a business model: the same chemical expertise that contaminated the land could be redirected to heal it, and controlling both processes was an unassailable market position. Thornback's early years were spent securing remediation contracts on worthless land, then purchasing that land once restored — a strategy that critics have called the most elegant land grab in modern history and that Adeyemi-Walsh's authorized biography describes simply as 'applied logic.' The corponation's most significant strategic asset is its monopoly on three proprietary soil amendment compounds — TB-7, TB-12, and TB-Rho — the only known treatments that can restore full agricultural productivity to heavy-metal-contaminated post-industrial soil. Roughly 60% of active corridor farmland requires at least one compound annually. Thornback refuses all licensing requests under Corridor Charter Article 19 sovereign IP protections. Its Field Security arm fields 11,000 personnel and surveillance drones repurposed for interdiction, backed by a chemical deterrence capability — the threatened sterilization of contested border soil — that has never required full execution. As a Big 20 member ranked food-security-critical, Thornback maintains a relationship with IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS and SULFUR CROWN AGRICULTURE that corridor economists have formally classified as structurally codependent mutual antagonism, a description all three parties have declined to dispute.

glmzTerritory.description: The Thornback Basin — 4,200 square kilometers of sovereign agricultural and industrial territory across the Door Peninsula and Fox River Valley, Zone 10. Agricultural chemistry, soil science, and specialty compound production derived from northern Great Lakes microbial ecosystems. Thornback maintains the Door Peninsula's farming communities as a managed resource under long-term supply agreements.
glmzTerritory.grayZoneRelationship: Door Peninsula rural communities exist in an ambiguous relationship with Thornback that resembles corponation tenancy without formal tier classification. Thornback prefers the ambiguity; it costs less than the alternative.
